about.title: Oxnard Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: A work injury in Oxnard rarely fits into one neat box. Maybe a forklift clipped you in a warehouse off Rose Avenue, or a delivery route down Saviers Road ended in a collision while you were on the clock. Workers' compensation covers medical care and part of your wages no matter who was at fault, and in most situations it is the only claim you can bring against your employer. What many Ventura County workers never hear is that someone other than the employer may also bear responsibility: a subcontractor who left a hazard in place, a property owner who ignored a broken stair, a manufacturer whose equipment failed, or another driver on Oxnard Boulevard. Those third-party claims are separate from comp, and they can address losses comp does not reach, such as pain and full lost earnings. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm. We match you with an independent attorney who looks at both paths and works on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Oxnard Workers Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: We look past the comp claim
items.desc: California law usually limits what you can seek from your employer, but a negligent subcontractor, property owner, equipment maker, or driver can be held separately accountable. The attorney you are matched with checks for that possibility early.

items.title: Deadlines are handled, not guessed at
items.desc: You generally have 30 days to report a work injury to your employer, and a third-party claim carries a two-year filing window. Getting connected quickly helps keep both on track.

items.title: Protection against retaliation
items.desc: Firing, demoting, or punishing a worker for reporting an injury or filing a claim is illegal in California. An independent attorney can explain your rights if pressure from an employer becomes a concern.

items.question: I was hit while driving for work on Ventura Road in Oxnard. Is that a workers' comp case or a car accident case?
items.answer: It can be both. Because you were on the job, workers' compensation applies regardless of who caused the crash. If another driver was negligent, you may also have a separate third-party claim against that driver, which is subject to California's two-year deadline. Oxnard recorded 857 injury collisions in 2025, with reports tending to peak on Fridays between 5 p.m. and 7 p.m., so work-related crashes are far from unusual here.

items.question: What if I waited a few weeks to tell my employer about the injury?
items.answer: California asks workers to report an injury to the employer within 30 days, so it is important to give written notice as soon as you can. A delay does not automatically end your options, but it can make things harder, especially if the injury developed gradually. An attorney can help you document when symptoms began and why reporting was delayed.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and we are not a law firm. The independent attorneys in our network handle workplace injury matters on contingency, which means you pay no attorney fee unless there is a recovery in your case.
